ucs.title: [LLM] Lazarus 'Operation DreamJob' — ISO/IMG container detonation chain (explorer → mounted-drive binary)
ucs.description: Catches the Lazarus DreamJob / TraderTraitor delivery pattern: a recruiter-themed ISO/IMG/VHD lands via browser or mail client, the victim double-clicks the auto-mounted virtual drive in Explorer, and a payload executes from a non-system drive letter — the precise mark-of-the-web bypass + DLL-side-load launcher chain documented by Mandiant, Microsoft (Diamond Sleet/ZINC) and CrowdStrike (Labyrinth Chollima) across the 2022-2024 fake-job campaigns.

ucs.kql:
let LookbackDays = 14d;
let IsoDrops = DeviceFileEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where ActionType == "FileCreated"
    | where FileName endswith ".iso" or FileName endswith ".img" or FileName endswith ".vhd" or FileName endswith ".vhdx"
    | where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","outlook.exe","thunderbird.exe","teams.exe","slack.exe")
    | project IsoTime=Timestamp, DeviceId, DeviceName,
              IsoUser=InitiatingProcessAccountName,
              IsoName=FileName, IsoSrcUrl=FileOriginUrl;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where FolderPath matches regex @"^[D-Z]:\\"   // payload executed from mounted ISO / removable
| where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "explorer.exe" // user double-click via shell
| where AccountName !endswith "$" and AccountName !in~ ("system","local service","network service")
| join kind=inner IsoDrops on DeviceId
| where Timestamp between (IsoTime .. IsoTime + 1h)   // detonation within 1h of drop
| extend DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, IsoTime)
| project IsoTime, ExecTime=Timestamp, DelaySec, DeviceName, AccountName,
          IsoName, IsoSrcUrl,
          SpawnedExe=FileName, SpawnedPath=FolderPath,
          ChildCmd=ProcessCommandLine, ChildSHA256=SHA256,
          ExeSignedBy=InitiatingProcessVersionInfoCompanyName
| order by IsoTime desc

ucs.title: [LLM] Lazarus FudModule / BYOVD — vulnerable-driver drop + kernel service registration
ucs.description: Catches the Lazarus FudModule rootkit deployment pattern: drop a known-vulnerable signed kernel driver (Dell dbutil, ENE, WinRing0, AppCheck, RTCore64, gdrv, mhyprot2, viragt64) followed by sc.exe / PowerShell service registration to load it. Microsoft (Diamond Sleet), AhnLab and ESET have all tied this exact BYOVD chain to Lazarus' EDR-tampering rootkit going back to the 2022 Dell-driver abuse and through 2024 appid.sys admin-to-kernel escalation.

let LookbackDays = 30d;
let SusDrivers = dynamic(["dbutil_2_3.sys","dbutildrv2.sys","ene.sys","winio.sys","winring0.sys","winring0x64.sys","appcheck.sys","gdrv.sys","rtcore64.sys","mhyprot2.sys","procexp152.sys","viragt64.sys","pkfltfs.sys"]);
let DriverDrops = DeviceFileEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where ActionType == "FileCreated"
    | where FileName has_any (SusDrivers)
    | where FolderPath has_any (@"\System32\drivers\", @"\SysWOW64\drivers\", @"\Windows\Temp\", @"\Users\Public\", @"\ProgramData\", @"\AppData\Local\Temp\")
    | project DropTime=Timestamp, DeviceId, DeviceName,
              DropperExe=InitiatingProcessFileName,

              DropperSHA256=InitiatingProcessSHA256,
              DropperUser=InitiatingProcessAccountName,
              DroppedDriver=FileName, DroppedPath=FolderPath, DroppedSHA256=SHA256;
DriverDrops
| join kind=leftouter (

          DropperExe, DropperPath, DropperCmd, DropperSHA256,
          SvcParent, SvcCmd
| order by DropTime desc

ucs.sigma_yaml:
title: Lazarus FudModule BYOVD - Known Vulnerable Driver Dropped
id: 7c1b1de4-3a7e-4f8a-b7b8-1a1f9a0e5d4d
status: experimental
description: Detects creation of a known vulnerable kernel driver in a location used by the Lazarus FudModule rootkit (Dell dbutil, ENE, WinRing0, AppCheck, RTCore64, gdrv, mhyprot2, viragt64). Microsoft (Diamond Sleet), AhnLab and ESET have tied this BYOVD set to Lazarus EDR-tampering activity since 2022.
references:
  - https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/blog/2024/05/16/threat-actors-misusing-quick-assist-in-social-engineering-attacks-leading-to-ransomware/
  - https://www.welivesecurity.com/2022/09/30/amazon-themed-campaigns-lazarus-netherlands-belgium/
  - https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0032/
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/16
tags:
  - attack.privilege_escalation
  - attack.defense_evasion
  - attack.t1068
  - attack.t1543.003
  - attack.t1562.001
  - attack.t1014
  - attack.g0032
logsource:
  category: file_event
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_name:
    TargetFilename|endswith:
      - '\dbutil_2_3.sys'
      - '\dbutildrv2.sys'
      - '\ene.sys'
      - '\winio.sys'
      - '\winring0.sys'
      - '\winring0x64.sys'
      - '\appcheck.sys'
      - '\gdrv.sys'
      - '\rtcore64.sys'
      - '\mhyprot2.sys'
      - '\procexp152.sys'
      - '\viragt64.sys'
      - '\pkfltfs.sys'
  selection_path:
    TargetFilename|contains:
      - '\System32\drivers\'
      - '\SysWOW64\drivers\'
      - '\Windows\Temp\'
      - '\Users\Public\'
      - '\ProgramData\'
      - '\AppData\Local\Temp\'
  filter_vendor:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\msiexec.exe'
      - '\TrustedInstaller.exe'
    Image|contains: '\Program Files\'
  condition: selection_name and selection_path and not filter_vendor
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate vendor installers running from \Program Files\ with valid signing chains - verify signer and parent process before dismissing.
level: high
